rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent low-rise bar-based composition across all four views, so it avoids the one-view-only failure and the visible-collision problem. It responds reasonably to the parcel and the frontage edge: the footprint stays contained, and the blue access edge is met by a legible seam/void rather than a sealed wall. The dominant gesture is understandable, but it is still somewhat over-fragmented into a compound of punched and split pieces, which weakens primary mass authority and makes the section feel less program-specific than the neighborhood-living brief prefers. Compared with the references, it resonates most with courtyard/bridge/interlocking low-rise precedents, but it does not yet achieve the same clarity of public void or a calm upper hierarchy. Program fit is plausible for neighborhood living because it can support active ground edge and mixed-use thresholds, though the section remains only moderately convincing as a capacity-aware street building. Overall: passable massing with useful void logic, but it should be simplified and given a cleaner anchor and stronger public court identity.
